Inkling 2 Mini: expert routing report

Can we tell what each expert is for?

Where the bytes of one generated token go

Weight and cache reads per decode token, from the trace and the GGUF tensor layout.

The loop reuses experts

Experts shared by the same token at the same physical block in two loop passes (decode, of 8). Random routing would share 0.5.

Reuse across tokens

Experts shared with the token lag steps earlier, same slot (decode).

Distinct experts for a batch of tokens

Expert slabs per slot needed by W consecutive decode tokens, vs. no sharing (W × 8).

Would a cache catch the reuse?

Byte hit rate of a fully associative cache over 14k decode tokens. L2 is 2 MB, the Infinity Cache (MALL) 32 MB.

Expert popularity

Share of each layer's routing decisions per expert (all prompts, all passes). A uniform router would give every cell 0.78%.

Specialists by prompt category

Layer-experts significantly enriched in a category (lift ≥ 1.5×, Benjamini-Hochberg q < 0.05, sequence-level permutation test).

How different is each category's routing?

Jensen-Shannon divergence (bits) of a category's expert distribution from all prompts, per layer.

Expert explorer

Category lift for every expert of one layer. Red = used more than average for that category, blue = less, gray ≈ average (colour smoothed for rarely used experts; exact values in the tooltip). A dot marks a significant enrichment. Click a column for the expert's profile.

Token-type specialists

The two strongest experts per token type (at least 50 expected selections). Tokens of that type are listed first; faded tokens are the expert's other favourites. Cyrillic, Arabic and Devanagari text each come from a single prompt, so treat those rows as anecdotes. Click a row to open its profile.
